title: What If Everyone Ate Insects Instead of Beef?

scenes.text: What if the whole world swapped beef for insects? Two billion people already eat them.
More than 1,900 insect species are eaten around the world, according to the UN's food agency.
Cattle need about 8 kilograms of feed to gain 1 kilogram. Insects need about 2.
A kilogram of beef is linked to about 14.8 kilograms of greenhouse gases.
Insects are rich in protein, fibre, iron and zinc, so the nutrition holds up.
So the swap would save a lot of feed. The hard part isn't science. It's persuading people to try it.
